analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: a date bump, the NemotronSuperServingPolicy.maximumEncodedBodyBytes value (8 MiB to 40 MiB, with a media_too_large error), and a note that a JSON response format may accompany tools. The two units I was given are base-side text at lines 1611-2365. They contain none of the changed ranges (base lines 3, 128-130, 528, 540-541), so I could not inspect the changed lines directly and relied on the patch excerpt, which is truncated (patch_excerpt_complete=false). The excerpt is documentation prose, so I cannot confirm from here that the source code matches it.

Open questions for the next pass:
- If the corresponding code raises the encoded-body ceiling from 8 to 40 MiB for Nemotron Super video/media, check that memory admission still applies (media-memory 503, shared budget charge, owner lock). The excerpt says these remain in place, and the policy touches TB-007 and T-029.
- The base-side text I examined makes no cache, attestation or key claims that this change would invalidate. The prefix-cache scoping statement (T-041, SEC-035) is unchanged, and the new tools-with-JSON note does not affect cache scope.
- I saw no new attack surface, secret exposure or threat-model assumption invalidated by the documentation. I set needs_deeper_review=true only because the code behind the documented 40 MiB limit is not in the supplied evidence.
